findings.title: RequireAdmin always returns true
findings.description: The RequireAdmin method returns true for both allowed and disallowed roles, effectively granting admin access to any authenticated session.

findings.title: Verify does not check token expiration
findings.description: The Verify method returns a session even if its ExpiresAt timestamp is in the past, allowing expired tokens to be used.

findings.title: BearerToken may throw IndexOutOfRange
findings.description: BearerToken splits the Authorization header and blindly accesses `parts[1]`. If the header is missing or malformed, this will throw.

findings.title: Issue can overwrite an existing session token
findings.description: `sessions[session.Token] = session;` overwrites any existing entry with the same token, potentially hijacking a session.

findings.title: Utilization uses integer division
findings.description: `return entries.Count / limit * 100;` performs integer division before multiplication, often yielding 0% for small caches.

findings.title: Sweep mutates dictionary during enumeration
findings.description: Iterating over `entries.Keys` while removing entries causes `InvalidOperationException`.

findings.title: Peek reports expired entries as cached
findings.description: `Peek` only checks key existence; it does not verify whether the entry has expired.

findings.title: Eviction does not follow LRU policy
findings.description: `Set` evicts `entries.Keys.First()` which is arbitrary, not the least‑recently‑used entry indicated by the comment.

findings.title: Timeout is set even when parsing fails
findings.description: If `LINKD_TIMEOUT_MS` cannot be parsed, `ms` remains 0 and the timeout is set to zero, violating the later validation.

findings.title: Cache TTL parsed using wrong time unit
findings.description: `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` is interpreted with `TimeSpan.FromSeconds`, treating milliseconds as seconds.

findings.title: `FETCH_LIMIT` environment variable is ignored
findings.description: The parsed value is stored in a local variable `parsed` but never assigned to `cfg.FetchLimit`.

findings.title: `Validate` always returns true
findings.description: Even when configuration problems are detected, the method returns `true`, allowing the service to start with invalid settings.

findings.title: `ExportCsvAsync` writes only header
findings.description: The async export function writes a static header and never includes the provided `links` data.

findings.title: `ExportCsvAsync` is declared `async void`
findings.description: `async void` methods swallow exceptions and cannot be awaited, making error handling unreliable.

findings.title: Quota increment may throw KeyNotFoundException
findings.description: `quota[owner] = quota[owner] + 1;` assumes the dictionary already contains the owner key.

findings.title: Resolve removes valid links and returns null
findings.description: The expiration check is inverted: it removes a link when it is still valid (`DateTime.Now < link.ExpiresAt`).

findings.title: `Rename` validates the source code twice
findings.description: Both validation calls use `ValidateCode(from)`, leaving the target code unchecked.

findings.title: `Page` off‑by‑one may cause `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`
findings.description: When `end > all.Count`, the code sets `end = all.Count + 1`, causing the range length to exceed the list size.

findings.title: `SuccessRate` integer division truncates result
findings.description: `used / links.Count * 100` performs integer division, often yielding 0% for small counts.

findings.title: `Top` sorts ascending, returning least‑used links
findings.description: The comparison `(a.Hits.CompareTo(b.Hits))` orders links from smallest to largest hits, contrary to the comment.

findings.title: `ByOwner` uses substring match
findings.description: `Owner.Contains(owner)` matches any owner whose name contains the query string, potentially returning unrelated owners.

findings.title: `Quotas` exposes internal mutable dictionary
findings.description: Returning the internal `quota` dictionary allows callers to modify it, violating the snapshot contract.

findings.title: `Prune` removes entries while iterating over keys
findings.description: Modifying `links` during enumeration throws `InvalidOperationException` and may leave the collection in an inconsistent state.

findings.title: `Prune` returns remaining count instead of removed count
findings.description: The method returns `links.Count` after pruning, which is the number of links left, not the number removed as described.

findings.title: `Delete` does not restore owner quota
findings.description: When a link is deleted the owner's quota is not decremented, causing quota counts to drift upward.

findings.title: `NewCode` may generate duplicate short codes
findings.description: `random.Next().ToString("x8")` can produce collisions, overwriting existing links.

findings.title: `AddCreated` is not thread‑safe
findings.description: `created++` is a non‑atomic increment and can lose counts under concurrent use.

findings.title: `StartJanitor` mutates store while enumerating keys
findings.description: Iterating over `store.All().Keys` and removing entries from the same dictionary causes `InvalidOperationException`.

findings.title: `CheckTargets` blocks on async call
findings.description: `ProbeAsync(...).Result` synchronously blocks on an async task, which can deadlock in certain contexts.

findings.title: `CountForOwner` throws if owner not present
findings.description: `store.Quotas()[owner]` assumes the owner key exists; missing owners cause `KeyNotFoundException`.

findings.title: Unsynchronized access to shared sessions dictionary
findings.description: The `sessions` dictionary is mutated in `Issue` (line 37) and `Revoke` (line 75) and iterated in `Verify` (line 48) without any locking or concurrent collection. Concurrent requests can cause race conditions, lost sessions, or `InvalidOperationException` during enumeration.

findings.title: Non‑thread‑safe `Random` used for token generation
findings.description: `Random` is not safe for concurrent use. Simultaneous calls to `Issue` can corrupt the RNG state, leading to duplicate or predictable tokens.

findings.title: `Peek` reads dictionary without synchronization
findings.description: `Peek` checks `entries.ContainsKey` without acquiring the lock used by `Set`, `Get`, and `Delete`. If another thread modifies `entries` concurrently, a race can produce incorrect results or throw.

findings.title: Removing entries while iterating over dictionary keys in `Sweep`
findings.description: `Sweep` iterates `foreach (var code in entries.Keys)` and removes entries inside the loop. Modifying a collection during enumeration throws `InvalidOperationException` and can leave the cache in an inconsistent state.

findings.title: File writes are not synchronized
findings.description: `ExportCsv` creates a new `StreamWriter` for a path derived from user input and writes without any coordination. Concurrent calls with the same `dir`/`name` can interleave writes, corrupting the CSV file or causing `IOException`.

findings.title: Shared temporary file in `WriteSnapshot` creates a race condition
findings.description: `WriteSnapshot` always writes to the same temporary path `"/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json"`. Parallel snapshot operations will race, overwriting each other's data and potentially leaving the final snapshot incomplete.

findings.title: `ExportCsvAsync` is declared `async void`
findings.description: `async void` fire‑and‑forget methods hide exceptions and cannot be awaited. If the asynchronous write fails, the failure is lost and the caller has no way to detect it.

findings.title: Unsynchronized mutation of `links` and `quota` dictionaries
findings.description: `Create` adds entries to `links` (line 40) and increments `quota[owner]` (line 41) without any locking. Simultaneous creates can corrupt the dictionaries, cause lost updates, or throw `KeyNotFoundException`.

findings.title: `Random` used for code generation is not thread‑safe
findings.description: `NewCode` calls `random.Next()` which is unsafe when multiple threads generate codes simultaneously, potentially producing duplicate or corrupted codes.

findings.title: `link.Hits++` is not atomic
findings.description: The `Resolve` method increments the `Hits` field without using atomic operations. Concurrent resolutions of the same code can lose increments, under‑reporting usage statistics.

findings.title: `Prune` removes entries while iterating over `links.Keys`
findings.description: `foreach (var code in links.Keys)` loop modifies `links` inside the body (`links.Remove(code)`). This triggers `InvalidOperationException` and can leave the store partially pruned.

findings.title: `Quotas` exposes internal mutable dictionary
findings.description: `Quotas` returns the raw `quota` dictionary, allowing callers to modify it without synchronization, which can corrupt quota counts when accessed concurrently.

findings.title: `SuccessRate` enumerates `links` without synchronization
findings.description: The method reads `links.Values` while other threads may add or remove entries, risking `InvalidOperationException` and inconsistent results.

findings.title: `Followed` returns a live enumerable over mutable dictionary values
findings.description: The returned `IEnumerable<Link>` captures `links.Values`. If the store is mutated after the call, enumerating the sequence can throw or yield inconsistent data.

findings.title: `AddCreated` increments a non‑atomic counter
findings.description: `created++` is not thread‑safe; concurrent calls can lose increments, causing an under‑count of created links.

findings.title: Janitor timer removes entries from `Store` without synchronization
findings.description: The timer callback iterates `store.All().Keys` and removes entries (`store.All().Remove(code)`) while other request handlers may be accessing or mutating the store. This can cause race conditions and `InvalidOperationException`.

findings.title: RequireAdmin always authorises
findings.description: Authenticator.RequireAdmin returns true unconditionally, even when the session role is not admin or owner. This allows any authenticated user to access admin‑only endpoints such as /admin/quotas.

findings.title: Predictable session tokens
findings.description: Session tokens are generated with `System.Random`, which is not cryptographically secure. An attacker can predict future tokens and hijack sessions.

findings.title: Hard‑coded development secret
findings.description: If the `LINKD_SECRET` environment variable is missing, the code falls back to the literal string `dev-secret-do-not-use`, which is a known secret and compromises authentication.

findings.title: Non‑constant‑time secret comparison
findings.description: `SecretEquals` uses `==` which can leak timing information about the matching prefix, enabling a timing side‑channel.

findings.title: Bearer token parsing can throw
findings.description: `BearerToken` splits the Authorization header and accesses `parts[1]` without validating that the header contains a space. A missing or malformed header throws `IndexOutOfRangeException`, leading to a denial‑of‑service.

findings.title: Delete endpoint lacks ownership check
findings.description: Authenticated users can delete any link by providing its code; the handler does not verify that the requesting session’s Owner matches the link’s Owner.

findings.title: Open redirect in /out endpoint
findings.description: The `next` query parameter is copied directly into the `Location` header without validation, allowing an attacker‑controlled redirect after authentication.

findings.title: Admin flag trusted without authentication
findings.description: `/admin/quotas` checks only the custom header `X-Admin` for the literal value `true`. Any client can set this header to gain admin information, especially because `RequireAdmin` is broken.

findings.title: Bearer token extraction used before validation
findings.description: `Authenticator.BearerToken` is called on whatever string is in the `Authorization` header, which can cause the earlier `IndexOutOfRangeException` and abort the entire request handling.

findings.title: Expired‑link logic inverted
findings.description: `Store.Resolve` removes a link when the current time is *before* its expiry and returns the target when the link is expired, effectively allowing usage of stale links while discarding fresh ones.

findings.title: Dictionary mutation during enumeration in Prune
findings.description: `Store.Prune` iterates over `links.Keys` and removes entries inside the loop, which throws `InvalidOperationException` and can crash the process.

findings.title: Janitor mutates store while iterating
findings.description: `Worker.StartJanitor` enumerates `store.All().Keys` and removes expired entries inside the same loop, causing the same `InvalidOperationException` and service downtime.

findings.title: Path traversal in CSV export
findings.description: The `name` parameter supplied by a user is concatenated with `Path.Combine(dir, name + ".csv")` without sanitisation. By including `../` or path separators, an attacker can cause the server to write files outside the intended export directory.

findings.title: Path traversal in CSV read
findings.description: `ReadReport` constructs the file path from an unvalidated `name` value in the same way as `ExportCsv`. An attacker can cause the service to read arbitrary CSV files within the export directory hierarchy.

findings.title: Symlink race on temporary snapshot file
findings.description: `WriteSnapshot` writes to a fixed temporary path `/tmp/linkd-snapshot.json` before moving it into place. An attacker who can create a symlink at that path could cause arbitrary file overwrite when the move occurs.

findings.title: Validate always returns true
findings.description: `Config.Validate` logs configuration problems but always returns `true`, so the service starts with invalid settings (e.g., out‑of‑range ports) that may expose insecure behaviour.

findings.title: Cache TTL interpreted as seconds instead of milliseconds
findings.description: `LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS` is parsed as an integer and assigned using `TimeSpan.FromSeconds`, treating the value as seconds. This makes TTLs up to 1000× longer than intended, potentially keeping stale data longer.

findings.title: Rename validates wrong variable and skips new code check
findings.description: `Store.Rename` calls `ValidateCode(from)` twice and never validates the destination code `to`. An attacker could rename a link to an invalid code that later bypasses validation checks.

findings.title: Off‑by‑one error in paging logic
findings.description: `Store.Page` sets `end = all.Count + 1` when `end > all.Count`, causing `GetRange` to request one element past the end of the list, which throws an exception and can be used for denial‑of‑service.
